title: A bill to require a regional strategy to address the threat posed by Boko Haram.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on September 22, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill requires:

  • the Department of State and the Department of Defense to develop jointly and submit to Congress a five-year strategy to help Nigeria, members of the Multinational Joint Task Force to Combat Boko Haram, and relevant partners to counter Boko Haram, and to assist Nigeria and its neighbors to address legitimate grievances of vulnerable populations in areas affected by Boko Haram; and
  • the Director of National Intelligence to assess the willingness and capability Nigeria and regional partners to implement such strategy.

Such strategy must address the following elements:

  • enhancing the institutional capacity, including military capabilities, of Nigeria and partner nations in the region to counter Boko Haram;
  • providing humanitarian support to civilian populations impacted by Boko Haram;
  • improving the capacity of Multinational Joint Task Force to Combat Boko Haram partner nations to investigate and prosecute human rights abuses by security forces and promote respect for the rule of law within the military;
  • assisting Nigeria and Multinational Joint Task Force to Combat Boko Haram nations to counter violent extremism;
  • strengthening the rule of law and Nigeria's capacity to enhance school security; and
  • identifying the resources required to achieve such objectives.

It is the sense of Congress that lack of economic opportunity and access to education, justice, and other social services contributes to Boko Haram's ability to radicalize and recruit individuals.

summary.headline: This law requires the State and Defense Departments to write a five-year plan for helping Nigeria and its neighbors counter the Boko Haram militant group.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Department of State and the Department of Defense to create and send to Congress a five-year strategy for countering Boko Haram in Nigeria and the surrounding region. The strategy must cover military training and capacity, humanitarian aid for affected civilians, human rights and rule-of-law efforts, countering violent extremism, and school security. The Director of National Intelligence must also assess whether Nigeria and regional partners are willing and able to carry out the plan. The law also states that Congress believes economic opportunity and access to education and justice help reduce recruitment by Boko Haram.

who_it_affects.group: Civilians in northeastern Nigeria and neighboring countries affected by Boko Haram
who_it_affects.how: The strategy must include humanitarian support for people harmed by the group's violence.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Multinational Joint Task Force to Combat Boko Haram
who_it_affects.how: The strategy is meant to help these partner nations build military capacity and improve how they handle human rights investigations.
The plan must address investigating and prosecuting human rights abuses by security forces and strengthening rule of law within the military.
The strategy must include efforts to strengthen school security in Nigeria.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on December 14, 2016, and the strategy is due to Congress after that; the source summary does not give an exact deadline.
